What is n8n?

Source-available workflow automation platform that can be self-hosted for free. Combines a visual node editor with the ability to drop into JavaScript or Python, and has become the default choice for building AI agent workflows with full data control.

Best for

Self-hosted AI agent and RAG workflows where data cannot leave your infrastructure.

Main features

  • Self-hostable (Docker, Kubernetes, npm) with no execution limits on the community edition
  • visual node editor plus custom code nodes
  • native LangChain integration for AI agent workflows
  • vector store nodes (Pinecone, Qdrant, Supabase, PGVector)
  • AI Agent node with tool calling
  • 1,000+ integrations plus universal HTTP node
  • sub-workflows
  • queue mode for scale
  • MCP client and server nodes.

Practical use cases

  • Building RAG pipelines and AI agents with full control over data
  • automating internal processes on-premises for compliance
  • orchestrating LLM calls across providers with fallback logic
  • replacing an expensive Zapier bill with self-hosted infrastructure.

Who is it for?

  • Developers, technical operations teams, AI engineers, and organisations with data-residency requirements.

Pricing, free access & limits

Free self-hosted (fair-code licence); paid cloud tiers by execution volume; enterprise self-hosted licence

Plans described in the source

Community Edition free and self-hosted with unlimited workflows and executions (Sustainable Use Licence - free for internal business use, restrictions on reselling as a service). n8n Cloud Starter from roughly EUR 20-24/mo (2,500 executions, 5 active workflows). Pro from roughly EUR 50-60/mo (10,000 executions, 15 active workflows). Enterprise custom, with SSO, LDAP, log streaming, air-gapped deployment and external secrets. Critically, n8n bills per workflow execution, not per step - a 50-step workflow counts as one execution.

Free plan

Yes - the self-hosted Community Edition is free and fully functional, which is the single biggest differentiator in this category.

Free trial

Yes - free trial of n8n Cloud; self-hosting is free indefinitely.

Usage limits to consider

Cloud tiers limit executions per month and the number of concurrently active workflows. Self-hosted has no vendor-imposed limits - only your own infrastructure capacity. The Sustainable Use Licence restricts offering n8n itself as a hosted service to third parties.

Strengths & tradeoffs

These points summarize the supplied research, rather than hands-on test results.

Strengths noted in the source

  • Per-execution rather than per-step billing makes it dramatically cheaper than Zapier at any real volume
  • self-hosting eliminates both cost and data-residency concerns
  • native LangChain and vector-store nodes make it the strongest platform here for building real AI agents
  • code nodes remove the no-code ceiling.

Limitations to consider

  • Genuinely requires technical skill - self-hosting means you own updates, backups, scaling and security
  • the licence is fair-code, not true open source, and restricts some commercial uses
  • UI is less polished than Make
  • fewer prebuilt connectors than Zapier
  • community support rather than SLA unless you buy enterprise.

Platforms, languages & integrations

Platforms

  • Self-hosted (Docker, Kubernetes, npm, Railway, Render)
  • n8n Cloud
  • desktop app

Languages

  • Interface in English and several community translations

API access

Yes - full REST API, webhooks, CLI, and a node SDK for building custom integrations

Integrations and exports

  • 1,000+ nodes including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Hugging Face, Pinecone, Qdrant, Supabase, Postgres, MySQL, Slack, Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, plus a universal HTTP node

Evaluation notes

The per-execution billing model is the headline economic advantage - a workflow with 50 nodes costs the same as one with 2. For any team with a developer and a compliance requirement, self-hosted n8n is usually the correct answer in this category.
